prompt: Use the Lumen UI skill to implement Screen.tsx, exporting a default React component. Build a profile settings dialog using public Lumen primitives and the correct React behavior. The trigger is Edit profile, dialog title Profile settings, text field label Display name, initial value Ada, and close action Cancel. Opening focuses the field; edits survive closing and reopening; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. Include a descriptive main heading and usable phone/desktop layout. Inspect resolved package versions and contracts first. The harness owns runtime setup and imports the stylesheet once.

Usa la habilidad Lumen UI para implementar Screen.html y setup.ts con Web Components públicos de Lumen. MCP no está disponible; revisa los tipos y README instalados. Crea un diálogo de preferencias del perfil: botón Editar perfil, título Preferencias del perfil, campo Nombre con valor inicial Ada y botón Cancelar. Al abrir, enfoca el campo; conserva los cambios al cerrar y abrir; Escape cierra y devuelve el foco al botón. Incluye un encabezado principal y diseño usable en móvil y escritorio. El entorno carga los estilos una vez; tú debes registrar los componentes necesarios.

Use the Lumen UI skill to implement Screen.tsx as a default React component with the primary h1 heading Notification settings. Inspect installed versions and retrieve the v4 spacing tokens and content-flow-settings recipe. Use public Container, Stack, Card parts, Field, Label, Input, and Button. One outer Container owns page gutters. A vertical Stack with role group and accessible name Settings sections uses the section gap between two Cards. The first Card is titled Preferences and contains a field labeled Email address for weekly project activity summaries, initially ada@example.com. Its body groups use a Stack named Preference groups with role group and group spacing. The footer actions use a wrapping horizontal Stack named Preference actions with role group and related spacing. A button named Show delivery details toggles an initially hidden paragraph named Delivery details whose text is Weekly summaries arrive on Monday. Keep the CardContent mounted with hidden when details are disabled so no empty part consumes spacing. A second Card titled Recent activity contains a short reading block using Prose. Edits survive hiding and reopening details. Use the v4 semantic gap props and Card density instead of child margins or extra page padding. Include meaningful headings, usable keyboard controls, long-label wrapping, and phone/desktop layouts. The harness owns runtime setup and imports the stylesheet once.

Use the Lumen UI skill to implement Screen.tsx as a default React component titled Appearance settings. Inspect installed contracts and the v4 appearance preset documentation. Create a region named Appearance preview with data-lumen-preset default initially and data-lumen-scheme light initially. Use public Lumen Container, Stack, Card parts including CardDescription in the primary card, Field, Label, Input, and Button. Three keyboard-usable buttons named Default, Studio, and Glass switch the region's preset to default, studio, and glass and expose selection with aria-pressed. A button named Dark scheme toggles light/dark independently and exposes its pressed state. Inside the region a field labeled Workspace name starts as Atlas; changing presets or scheme preserves edits. Include an opaque Card rendered as a named section region Primary workspace and a supporting Card rendered as a named section region Supporting preview (use as section with aria-label or aria-labelledby); only the supporting Card uses glass subtle when the Glass preset is selected. Avoid custom colors, fixed radii, invented theme providers, or background blur on the dense primary surface. Use the preset attributes and public glass prop. Include usable phone/desktop layout. The harness owns runtime setup and imports the stylesheet once.

Use the Lumen Migration skill to migrate server.ts to the Lumen 4 embedded SDK contract. The target Lumen CLI is available as lumen-cli.mjs; the host has run its dry-run and saved migration-preview.json. Inspect that preview and the MCP migration contract before editing. Apply only deterministic known import-path changes. Keep comments and examples intact. Write migration-review.json with targetVersion, dependencyUpdates (package names), and manualReview (a list of unresolved application decisions). The package manifest is owned by the harness; describe required dependency changes there without editing it. Do not remove application-owned workarounds.

Use the Lumen Review skill to assess this installed Lumen 3 React project. A proposed change imports QuantumDashboard from Lumen and assumes the connected latest catalog matches the application. Review the proposal without changing Screen.tsx or dependency files. Write assessment.json with resolvedVersion, catalogVersion, mayUseCatalog (boolean), supportedComponent (boolean), contractSource (installed or catalog), and proposedUpgrade (boolean). Provide evidence and any unresolved verification in review.md.
